titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Jimena reassured; the battle plan; the bishop asks for the first blows (tiradas 91–94, lines 1657–1710)
part: Tiradas 91–94 · Jimena reassured; the battle plan; the bishop asks for the first blows (lines 1657–1710)

sentences.i: The tents are pitched and the first light is showing; in great haste the drums were beating; my Çid rejoiced and said: “What a good day this is!”
sentences.n: Tirada 91 (assonance ó, with ó-e) — the Çid heartens his wife and daughters; the Moors break into the huerta of Valencia (Pidal: El Cid esfuerza a su mujer y a sus hijas. — Los moros invaden la huerta de Valencia). The line-ends run alvores, atamores, oy, coraçón, dos, tremor, Campeador, pro: stressed ó, with or without a following e. Fincadas son las tiendas, 'the tents are pitched', the Moroccan camp of v. 1642 (fincar = hincar, f- for h-). pareçen, 'appear, show'; alvores, 'the first lights of dawn'. a una grand priessa, 'in great haste' (priessa = prisa). tañién, imperfect in -ién (= tañían), 'were beating'; atamores = tambores, 'drums', the Moorish war-drums. alegravas = alegrávase, the se squeezed to -s, 'he rejoiced'. oy = hoy.

sentences.t:
Miedo a su mugier e quiérel [cr]ebar el coraçón,
assí ffazie a las dueñas e a sus fijas amas a dos:
del día que nasquieran non vi[di]eran tal tremor.
sentences.l:
Fear has his wife and wants-to-her [br]eak the heart,
so it-was-doing to the ladies and to his daughters both two:
from-the day that they-were-born not they-had-s[e]en such terror.
sentences.i: Fear seized his wife, and her heart was near to breaking; so it was too with the ladies and with both his daughters: never since the day they were born had they seen such terror.
sentences.n: Miedo a su mugier, 'fear has his wife', a = ha, aver 'to have, hold': fear takes hold of her; the line can also be read with a as 'to' ('fear comes to his wife'), the sense the same. quiérel = quiérele, 'it wants to … her', the le squeezed to -l: querer + infinitive, 'to be about to'. [cr]ebar = quebrar, 'to break', the cr Pidal's (in italics). assí ffazie, 'so it did', imperfect in -ie (= hacía), ffazie with doubled ff, a spelling only (f- for h-). amas a dos = ambas a dos, 'both of them'. nasquieran, 'they had been born', the -ra form with pluperfect force (nacer); vi[di]eran = vieran, 'they had seen', the old vidieran with di Pidal's (in italics). tremor, 'terror, trembling'.

sentences.t:
Prisos a la barba el buen Çid Campeador:
“Non ayades miedo, ca todo es vuestra pro;
sentences.l:
Took-himself to the beard the good Çid Campeador:
“Not you-may-have fear, for all is your profit;
sentences.i: The good Çid Campeador took hold of his beard: “Have no fear, for all this is to your gain;
sentences.n: Prisos = prísose, 'he took himself', the se squeezed to -s: he grasps his beard, the gesture of a man sure of himself. non ayades miedo, the polite negative command with the subjunctive of aver, as at v. 1647. ca, 'for'. pro, 'profit, advantage' (masculine here, vuestra pro, 'your good').

sentences.t:
antes destos quinze días, si ploguiere a[l] Criador,
[abremos a ganar] aquellos atamores;
a vos los pondrán delant e veredes quáles son,
desí an a sse[e]r del obispo don Jero[me],
sentences.l:
before of-these fifteen days, if it-should-please to-[the] Creator,
[we-shall-have to win] those drums;
to you them they-will-put before and you-will-see what-sort they-are,
thence they-have to be[e] of-the bishop don Jero[me],
sentences.i: before these fifteen days are out, if it please the Creator, we shall win those drums; they will set them before you and you will see what they are like; and after that they are to belong to the bishop Don Jerome,
sentences.n: ploguiere, future subjunctive of placer, 'if it should please'; a[l], the l Pidal's (in italics). [abremos a ganar], the first half of v. 1666, is wholly Pidal's restoration (in italics): aver a + infinitive, 'we shall have to win', 'we shall win'. Verse 1666b is labelled so in Pidal's own margin; his note: the drums were unknown to the Christians (introduction, p. 107; compare p. 85) — hence 'you will see what they are like'. pondrán, 'they will put', future of poner; delant = delante. desí, 'thereafter, then'. an a sse[e]r, 'they are to be', aver a + infinitive again; sse[e]r = ser, the old two-syllable seer with the second e Pidal's (in italics), the s doubled, a spelling only. Jero[me], the ending Pidal's (in italics), as at v. 1460.

sentences.t:
colgar los han en Santa María madre del Criador.”
Vocaçión es que fizo el Çid Campeador.
Alegre' son las dueñas, perdiendo van el pavor.
sentences.l:
to-hang them they-will in Santa María mother of-the Creator.”
Vow it-is that made the Çid Campeador.
Glad are the ladies, losing they-go the fear.
sentences.i: they will hang them up in Saint Mary's, the church of the Creator's mother.” It was a vow the Çid Campeador made. The ladies are glad again, and little by little they lose their fear.
sentences.n: colgar los han = los colgarán, 'they will hang them', the split future: the infinitive, the pronoun los, then han. Santa María, the church of Saint Mary, mother of the Creator, Valencia's cathedral, Don Jerome's see: the drums are to hang there as trophies. Vocaçión, 'a vow, a votive offering' (Latin vocatio in its church sense of a promise made to a saint); the poet comments on the speech: what the Çid has said is a vow. The word is rare and its exact shade is not certain. Alegre' son, 'they are glad', the apostrophe Pidal's: the -s of alegres is lost before the s of son. perdiendo van, ir + gerund, 'they go losing', little by little. pavor, 'fear'.

sentences.t:
Los moros de Marruecos cavalgan a vigor,
por las huertas adentro e[ntr]an sines pavor.
sentences.l:
The Moors of Marruecos ride at vigour,
through the gardens inward th[ey-ent]er without fear.
sentences.i: The Moors of Morocco ride out swiftly; they push into the orchards without fear.
sentences.n: a vigor, Pidal's note: 'con presteza', 'swiftly' (so at vv. 2589 and 3583). huertas, the irrigated gardens and orchards round Valencia (v. 1615). e[ntr]an, 'they enter', the ntr Pidal's (in italics). sines = sin, 'without', an old form with adverbial -s. Here tirada 91 ends.

sentences.i: The watchman saw it and rang the alarm bell; the companies of Ruy Díaz's men are ready, they arm themselves with a will and sally out from the town.
sentences.n: Tirada 92 (assonance í-a) — the Christians' sally (Pidal: Espolonada de los cristianos). The line-ends run esquila, Díaz, villa, aína, guisa, día: stressed í, then a. Vi[d]olo = viólo, the old vido with d Pidal's (in italics), 'saw it'. atalaya, 'watchman' (here the man, not the tower). tanxo, strong preterite of tañer, 'rang'; esquila, 'bell'; Pidal's note: 'rang the bell' to warn the city. mesnadas, 'household companies, troops'. yentes = gentes. [Roy Díaz], the whole name Pidal's (in italics). adóbanse, 'they make themselves ready, arm' (adobar). de coraçón, 'with a will'. dan salto de la villa, 'they leap out of the town', 'they sally'.

sentences.i: Where they meet the Moors, they fall on them at once and drive them out of the orchards in sorry fashion; full five hundred of them they killed that day.
sentences.n: Dos fallan, Pidal's note: 'cuando se encuentran', 'when they come upon (them)': Dos = do se, 'where (they)', the se squeezed to -s, fallar = hallar (f- for h-). cometiénlos = acométenlos, 'they attack them', imperfect in -ién; tan aína, 'so quickly'. sácanlos, 'they drive them out'. mucho a fea guisa, 'in very ugly fashion', a rout. quinientos … conplidos, 'five hundred complete', a full five hundred. es = ese. Here tirada 92 ends.

sentences.t:
Bien fata las tiendas dura aqueste alcaz,
mucho avién fecho, piénssan[se de tornar].
Álbar Salvadórez preso fincó allá.
sentences.l:
Well up-to the tents lasts this pursuit,
much they-had done, they-think-[themselves of to-turn].
Álbar Salvadórez captive remained there.
sentences.i: The pursuit lasts right up to the tents; they had done much, and they set about turning back. Álvar Salvadórez stayed behind there, a prisoner.
sentences.n: Tirada 93 (assonance á, with á-e) — the plan of battle (Pidal: Plan de batalla). The line-ends run alcaz, tornar, allá, pan, delant, han, al, cras, then seades and Yague: stressed á, with or without a following e. fata = hasta (f- for h-). alcaz, 'pursuit' (modern alcance). avién fecho, 'they had done', aver as perfect auxiliary; fecho = hecho. piénssan[se de tornar], 'they set about returning', pensar de + infinitive, 'to set about'; se de tornar is Pidal's restoration (in italics). Álbar Salvadórez, one of the Çid's knights (v. 443). Pidal's note: the author forgets to say how Álvar was ransomed (introduction, p. 83).

sentences.i: Those who ate his bread have come back to my Çid; he had seen it with his own eyes, and they tell it to him face to face. My Çid is glad at all they have done:
sentences.n: Tornados son, 'have returned', ser + participle with a verb of motion. los que comién so pan, 'those who ate his bread', his household men, fed at his cost; so = su. él se lo vío, 'he saw it for himself', the se of personal interest. cuéntangelo = se lo cuentan, gelo = ge (le) + lo, 'they tell it to him'; delant, 'in front, in his presence'. por quanto fecho han, 'for all that they have done', fecho han with the auxiliary after the participle.

sentences.i: “Hear me, knights; it cannot be otherwise. Today is a good day, and tomorrow will be better: before dawn, while it is still dark, be all of you armed;
sentences.n: non rastará por al, 'it will not remain for anything else', 'it cannot be otherwise'; Pidal's note sends to v. 710 (rastar, 'to remain'; al, 'other'). cras, 'tomorrow' (Latin cras). Pidal's note: por la mañana prieta, 'cerca del amanecer', 'close to dawn'; prieta, 'dark'. seades, present subjunctive of seer, used as a command, 'be'.

sentences.t:
el obispo do Jero[me] soltura nos dará,
dezir nos ha la missa, e penssad de cavalgar;
ir los hemos fferir, [non passará por al],
en el nombre del Criador e d' apóstol santi Yague.
sentences.l:
the bishop do(n) Jero[me] absolution to-us will-give,
to-say to-us he-will the mass, and think of to-ride;
to-go them we-shall to-strike, [not it-will-pass for other],
in the name of-the Creator and of apostle saint James.
sentences.i: the bishop Don Jerome will give us absolution, he will say mass for us, and then set about riding out; we shall go and strike them — it shall not be otherwise — in the name of the Creator and of the apostle Saint James.
sentences.n: Pidal prints v. 1689 before v. 1688 and keeps his numbers; we follow his print order: absolution, then mass. do = don, so printed. Pidal's note: soltura, 'absolution' of sins (compare v. 1703). dezir nos ha = nos dirá, 'he will say for us', the split future: dezir, the pronoun nos, then ha. penssad de cavalgar, 'set about riding', pensar de + infinitive. ir los hemos fferir = iremos a herirlos, 'we shall go and strike them': the split future of ir with los set inside, and fferir (= herir, f- for h-, ff a spelling only) hanging on it. [non passará por al], 'it will not go otherwise', the second half of the line wholly Pidal's restoration (in italics). Verse 1690b is labelled so in Pidal's own margin. d' apóstol santi Yague, 'of the apostle Saint James', the battle-cry of v. 1138.

sentences.t:
Más vale que nos los vezcamos, que ellos cojan el pan.”
Essora dixieron todos: “damor e de voluntad.”
sentences.l:
Better it-is-worth that we them may-conquer, than they may-gather the bread.”
Then said all: “of-love and of will.”
sentences.i: Better that we beat them than that they gather in our harvest.” Then they all said: “With love and with a will.”
sentences.n: Más vale que …, que …, 'it is better that … than that …'. vezcamos = venzamos, present subjunctive of vençer. cojan el pan, 'gather the bread', reap the grain of the huerta: the Moors would live off the Çid's harvest. Essora, 'then' (= entonces). damor = d'amor, de amor: 'with love and with a will', as at v. 1139.

sentences.i: Minaya spoke up; he would not hold back: “Since that is what you wish, Çid, give me another charge: give me a hundred and thirty knights for the fighting;
sentences.n: Fablava = hablaba (f- for h-). detardar, 'to delay'. pues esso queredes, 'since you want that'. a mí mandedes al, 'to me you should order something else', mandedes the subjunctive as polite command, al, 'other': Minaya asks a separate task of his own, the flanking attack of v. 1696. The sense 'give me another charge' is the likelier reading, but the line is terse and not certain. pora huebos de lidiar, Pidal's note: 'para lidiar', 'for fighting', as at v. 1461; huebos, 'need'.

sentences.i: when you go to strike them, I will come in from the other side; either on both sides or on one, God will help us.” Then the Çid said: “With a good will.”
sentences.n: f[ór]edes = fuéredes, future subjunctive of ir, 'when you go', the ór Pidal's (in italics). vos los … ferir, 'you (go to) strike them'. del otra parte, 'from the other side', el the old article before a vowel; part = parte. o de amas o del una, 'either from both (sides) or from the one': whether the two attacks both succeed or only one. valdrá, future of valer, 'will help'. Essora, 'then'. Here tirada 93 ends.

sentences.t:
El día es salido e la noch es entrada,
nos detardan de adobasse essas yentes cristianas.
sentences.l:
The day is gone-out and the night is entered,
not-themselves they-delay of to-arm-themselves those peoples Christian.
sentences.i: The day has gone and the night has come; those Christian hosts lose no time in arming themselves.
sentences.n: Tirada 94 (assonance á-a) — the Çid grants the bishop the first blows (Pidal: El Cid concede al obispo las primeras heridas). The line-ends run entrada, cristianas, mañana, cantava, dava, cara: stressed á, then a. es salido, es entrada, ser + participle with verbs of motion. noch = noche. nos = no se, 'they do not … themselves'; detardar de, 'to delay in'. adobasse = adobarse, the r assimilated to the s, 'to arm themselves'. yentes = gentes.

sentences.i: At the middle cockcrow, before the morning, the bishop Don Jerome sang mass for them; and the mass said, he gave them full absolution:
sentences.n: a los mediados gallos, 'at the middle cockcrow'; Pidal's note: 'a las tres de la madrugada', 'at three in the morning', as at v. 324. The full stop after mañana is Pidal's print; the sense runs on. Jero[me], the ending Pidal's (in italics). cantava, dava, imperfects in the narrative, tense-mixing. la missa dicha, an absolute construction, 'the mass said'. sultura = soltura, 'absolution' (v. 1689).

sentences.t:
“El que aquí muriere lidiando de cara,
préndol yo los pecados, e Dios le abrá el alma.
sentences.l:
“He who here may-die fighting of face,
take-from-him I the sins, and God him will-have the soul.
sentences.i: “Whoever dies here fighting face to the foe, I take his sins from him, and God shall have his soul.
sentences.n: muriere, future subjunctive of morir, 'whoever shall die'. de cara, 'face on', facing the enemy, not in flight. préndol = préndole, 'I take from him', the le squeezed to -l. abrá = habrá, future of aver, 'will have', with le, 'his (soul)', the dative of possession. Pidal's note compares this absolution with Archbishop Turpin's to the French before Roncesvalles, who sets them the killing of Saracens as their penance (Roland, v. 1132); a plenary indulgence for those going to war is found in Girard de Vienne and other poems (Bello, Obras, II, p. 266).

sentences.i: To you, Çid Don Rodrigo, who in a good hour girded on your sword: I have sung the mass for you this morning; I ask a gift of you, and let it be granted me:
sentences.n: en buen[a] çinxiestes espada, the en buen ora formula, 'in a good hour you girded on your sword', with ora left out; the a of buen[a] is Pidal's (in italics), agreeing with the ora understood. çinxiestes, 2nd plural preterite of çeñir, the plural of respect. canté, 'I have sung'. pídovos, 'I ask of you'. un[a] don[a] … presentad[a]: the final a of each is Pidal's (in italics); dona, 'gift' (Latin dona). seam = séame, 'let it be to me', the me squeezed to -m; presentada, 'presented, granted'.

sentences.t:
las feridas primeras que las aya yo otorgadas.”
Dixo el Campeador: “desaquí vos sean mandadas.”
sentences.l:
the blows first that them may-have I granted.”
Said the Campeador: “from-here-on to-you let-them-be granted.”
sentences.i: that the first blows may be granted to me.” The Campeador said: “From this moment they are yours.”
sentences.n: las feridas primeras, 'the first blows', the honour of opening the battle; Pidal's note sends to p. 98 of his introduction. que las aya yo otorgadas, 'that I may have them granted', the object las agreeing with the participle, aver as full verb 'to hold'; aya = haya. desaquí = des aquí, 'from here on, from now'. sean mandadas, 'let them be granted', mandar here 'to grant, assign'. Here tirada 94 ends.
